headline: 839 hospitalised in 24 hours as dengue cases hit yearly high
summary: Five more people died in a single day, bringing the total death toll to 82 and total cases to 28,929 this year.
details: At least five dengue patients died and 839 others were hospitalised in the 24 hours till yesterday morning. This marks the highest single-day hospitalisation count recorded so far this year.

Of the deceased, three were from Dhaka South City Corporation, while one each was from the Dhaka and Khulna divisions. The total number of dengue deaths has now risen to 82, with total cases reaching 28,929.
Currently, 1,951 dengue patients are undergoing treatment in hospitals across the country. Experts warn that cases will likely continue to rise through October before declining in November.
Prof Kabirul Bashar of Jahangirnagar University stressed the need to identify neighbourhood-level hotspots and intensify mosquito control and community awareness campaigns.
He also recommended focusing on source reduction and larviciding activities at the national level to curb mosquito breeding.
Medical experts advise patients to undergo evaluations at the onset of fever, on the third or fourth day, and again after the fever subsides.
Immediate medical attention is urged if warning signs appear, such as severe abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, breathing difficulties, or bleeding.
caption:
839 people hospitalised in just 24 hours. Dengue cases have hit a yearly high in Bangladesh.

At least five dengue patients died and 839 others were hospitalised in the 24 hours till yesterday morning. This marks the highest single-day hospitalisation count recorded so far this year.

Of the deceased, three were from Dhaka South City Corporation, while one each was from the Dhaka and Khulna divisions. The total number of dengue deaths has now risen to 82, with total cases reaching 28,929.

Currently, 1,951 dengue patients are undergoing treatment in hospitals across the country. Experts warn that cases will likely continue to rise through October before declining in November.

Prof Kabirul Bashar of Jahangirnagar University stressed the need to identify neighbourhood-level hotspots and intensify mosquito control and community awareness campaigns.

He also recommended focusing on source reduction and larviciding activities at the national level to curb mosquito breeding.

Medical experts advise patients to undergo evaluations at the onset of fever, on the third or fourth day, and again after the fever subsides.

Immediate medical attention is urged if warning signs appear, such as severe abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, breathing difficulties, or bleeding.

headline: 21 former cricket captains urge humane treatment for Imran Khan
summary: Legends like Greg Chappell, Sunil Gavaskar, and Kapil Dev have written to Pakistan's PM, demanding proper medical care for the imprisoned former leader.
details: Former Australia captain Greg Chappell, along with 20 other international captains including India's Sunil Gavaskar and Kapil Dev, has appealed to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif for the 'humane treatment and proper medical care' of Imran Khan.
caption:
Cricket legends unite: 21 former captains demand humane treatment for Imran Khan.

Former Australia captain Greg Chappell, along with 20 other international captains including India's Sunil Gavaskar and Kapil Dev, has appealed to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif for the 'humane treatment and proper medical care' of Imran Khan.
